correctness.summary: The bitset word-count `size = (target+63)>>6` is one word too small whenever `target` is an exact multiple of 64. The word that holds the target bit (index `target>>6`) is then never allocated/processed, and the final check `targetIdx < size` is false, so the method always returns 0 even when the subset sum is achievable.
correctness.triggeringInput: n=1, target=64, a=[64], bits buffer of size>=1. Expected result 1 (subset {64} sums to 64); method returns 0. Same for target=128 a=[64,64], or any reachable target that is a multiple of 64.
correctness.rootCause: To hold bits 0..target inclusive you need (target>>6)+1 words (the bit `target` lives in word index target>>6, and word indices are 0-based). The formula (target+63)>>6 = ceil((target+1)/64) only equals (target>>6)+1 when target is NOT a multiple of 64; when target%64==0 it yields target/64, which is one word short. Consequently bits[targetIdx] is outside the [0,size) range the routine zeroes and updates, BitsetShiftOr's loop `j>=offset` skips the missing top word, and the return guard `targetIdx < size` (1<1) fails, forcing a 0 result.
correctness.suggestedFix: Compute the word count as `int size = (int)((target >> 6) + 1);` (equivalently (target/64)+1) so the word containing bit `target` is always included; the caller's `bits` buffer must be sized accordingly. The shift-OR carry logic itself is correct and needs no change.

perf.summary: dp is indexed with (int) casts of long loop counters; the casts add work and force int-domain arithmetic on indices that are already known non-negative longs.
perf.currentCost: Each inner-loop access dp[(int)(c - weight)] and dp[(int)c] performs a long->int narrowing conversion (movsxd/cdqe-class), and the subtraction c-weight is recomputed as long then narrowed every iteration.
perf.proposedChange: Drive the inner loop with a native-width index (nint/long) and keep dp[idx] in the long domain so no per-iteration (int) cast is emitted. Hoist the read of dp[(int)(c-weight)] vs dp[(int)c]: iterate c from cap down to weight using two running pointers (long* cur=dp+c, long* prev=dp+c-weight) decremented together, eliminating both the subtraction and both casts per iteration.
perf.rationale: Pointer-walk form removes one subtraction and two narrowing casts per iteration in the hottest loop (O(n*cap)), shortening the dependency chain to a compare+cmov+store. dp index domain stays identical so addresses are unchanged.
perf.risk: None for valid input: cap and c-weight are non-negative and < array length by contract, so the int cast was already lossless; pointer form yields identical addresses. Ensure pointers use the same element type (long) to keep scaling correct.

perf.summary: Branchy max update (if val > dp[c]) prevents Burst from emitting a branchless cmov and may mispredict on adversarial weight/value patterns.
perf.currentCost: Per iteration: compare + conditional store with a data-dependent branch; mispredicts flush the pipeline.
perf.proposedChange: Replace 'long val = prev+value; if (val > cur) cur = val;' with 'dp[c] = math.max(dp[c], prev+value);' (branchless). Under Burst, math.max(long,long) lowers to compare+cmov; even hand-written 'cur ^= (cur ^ val) & -(long)(val>cur)' is branchless but math.max is cleaner.
perf.rationale: Removes a data-dependent branch from an O(n*cap) loop, converting it to straight-line code Burst can pipeline/vectorize-friendlier. Identical result.
perf.risk: Semantically identical (max). The XOR-mask trick relies on (val>cur) producing 0/1 then negation to all-ones; prefer math.max to avoid sign/overflow subtlety. No behavior change.

perf.summary: Loop nesting is inverted vs the cache-friendly form: outer over capacity, inner over items, so w[i]/v[i] are re-streamed for every one of the `cap` capacities, and the (int) casts plus per-iteration w[i] reload dominate.
perf.currentCost: O(cap*n) with item arrays w[]/v[] fully re-read cap times (poor temporal locality of the item stream), plus a branch 'if (w[i] <= c)' and three (int) casts per accepted item.
perf.proposedChange: Invert loops to outer-over-items, inner-over-capacity (the standard unbounded form): for each item, for c = w[i] .. cap: dp[c] = max(dp[c], dp[c-w[i]] + v[i]). This streams w[i]/v[i] once per item (kept in registers across the whole inner sweep), removes the per-iteration 'w[i] <= c' branch (loop starts at w[i]), and lets the inner loop use a pointer walk to drop the (int) casts. Result is identical because unbounded knapsack is order-independent over the forward sweep.
perf.rationale: Hoists w[i]/v[i] out of the inner loop (loop-invariant for the inner sweep), removes a branch, improves locality of dp[] sequential access, and removes casts. Same asymptotic class but far better constant factor and cache behavior.
perf.risk: Must keep the FORWARD sweep (c increasing) for unbounded semantics — that is what allows reusing the current item multiple times. Behavior is identical to the current code, which also reuses items within the same c. No overflow change.

perf.summary: Bounded knapsack uses naive per-cap multiplicity scan: O(cap * maxUse) per item, giving O(n * cap * count) overall. Binary (power-of-two) decomposition reduces it to O(n * cap * log(count)).
perf.currentCost: ProcessBoundedItem's count>1 path runs, for each of cap+1 capacities, an inner loop up to maxUse iterations each doing k*weight and k*value multiplies — O(cap*maxUse) per item, multiplications recomputed every k.
perf.proposedChange: Decompose count into powers of two (1,2,4,...,remainder) and run a standard 0/1 update for each piece with combined weight=p*weight, value=p*value. This turns each item into O(log count) virtual items, each an O(cap) 0/1 sweep: total O(n*cap*log count) instead of O(n*cap*count). Also eliminates the inner k*weight/k*value multiplies (precompute pieceWeight/pieceValue once per piece).
perf.rationale: Asymptotically tighter for count>1 and removes repeated multiplications; the 0/1 sweep is the already-optimized branchless/pointer-walk loop. Standard, provably equivalent bounded-knapsack result.
perf.risk: Must reuse the existing 0/1 sweep semantics (descending c) for each piece. Watch overflow: p*value can be large — but it is <= count*value which the current code already computes (k*value up to maxUse*value), so no new overflow domain. Equivalent optimal value guaranteed by binary representation completeness.

perf.summary: The count>1 path iterates c from cap down to 0, but for c < weight the inner UpdateBoundedCap loop body 'c >= k*weight' (k starts at 1) is always false, doing useless iterations.
perf.currentCost: For c in [0, weight-1] the outer loop still calls UpdateBoundedCap which immediately fails its guard; that is up to `weight` wasted outer iterations per item plus call overhead (if not inlined).
perf.proposedChange: Lower bound the outer loop to c >= weight (for (long c = cap; c >= weight; c--)), since no k>=1 can satisfy c >= k*weight when c < weight. If the binary-decomposition rewrite above is adopted this method disappears; otherwise this guard is a free win.
perf.rationale: Eliminates up to `weight` no-op outer iterations and their call/guard overhead per bounded item. Identical result.
perf.risk: None: when c < weight the original inner loop produced no writes, so skipping those c values changes nothing.

perf.summary: Inner loop recomputes k*weight and k*value each iteration via multiplication.
perf.currentCost: Two long multiplies per k (k*weight, k*value) plus the cast (int)(c - k*weight) each iteration.
perf.proposedChange: Strength-reduce to running accumulators: 'long cw = weight, cv = value;' then each iteration use cw/cv and do 'cw += weight; cv += value;'. Replaces two multiplies/iteration with two adds. (Moot if binary decomposition is adopted, which removes this loop entirely.)
perf.rationale: Add is cheaper than imul and shortens the dependency chain; identical values produced.
perf.risk: None for valid input; accumulator path reaches the same cw=k*weight, cv=k*value values. Overflow domain unchanged (same maximum products as multiply form).

perf.summary: A dedicated bool[] DP is used while BitsetSubsetSum already provides a 64x-denser, ~64x-faster bitset variant; the bool variant is redundant and the slowest path for reachability.
perf.currentCost: bool* dp uses target+1 bytes and the inner loop processes one capacity per iteration with a data-dependent branch (if dp[s-val]) — O(n*target) byte stores, 64x more memory traffic than the bitset.
perf.proposedChange: For the reachability (subset-sum boolean) use case, route callers to BitsetSubsetSum (already present), or at minimum document SubsetSum as the simple/reference path. If SubsetSum.Run must stay, make its inner store branchless: 'dp[(int)s] |= dp[(int)(s-val)];' (OR into target) instead of 'if (dp[s-val]) dp[s]=true;', removing the branch.
perf.rationale: Bitset form is 64x less RAM and ~64x fewer operations for the identical reachability answer; even keeping the bool form, the branchless OR removes a misprediction-prone branch in the O(n*target) loop.
perf.risk: Branchless OR is semantically identical for bool (true stays true, only sets when source true). Steering to bitset is an API/ergonomics change for callers, not a behavior change in the result bit.

perf.summary: Hot shift loop recomputes the carry index check 'j - offset - 1 >= 0' as a branch inside the per-word loop.
perf.currentCost: Per word j: a branch 'if (j - offset - 1 >= 0)' guarding the carry-in OR. The guard only fails for the single lowest word (j == offset); branching every iteration to handle one boundary word.
perf.proposedChange: Peel the boundary: run the main loop for j from size-1 down to offset+1 doing the full two-term OR unconditionally (j-offset-1 >= 0 always holds there), then handle j == offset separately with only the 'bits[j] |= bits[0] << shift' term. Removes the per-iteration boundary branch.
perf.rationale: Eliminates a branch from the inner O(size) word loop (run n times => O(n*size) overall); the peeled iteration runs once per item. Identical bit result.
perf.risk: None: the peeled j==offset case omits exactly the carry term that the original guard already skipped (since j-offset-1 = -1 < 0). Word ordering of the OR-into-self descending sweep is preserved, so no read-after-write hazard is introduced.

perf.summary: RunSpaceEfficient is an exact alias of Run (already 1D/space-efficient), implying a distinction that does not exist and risking caller confusion.
perf.currentCost: Two public symbols with identical behavior; no perf cost but discoverability/maintenance cost and an implied 2D-vs-1D contract that isn't real.
perf.proposedChange: Either remove RunSpaceEfficient (Run is already the space-efficient 1D form) or document explicitly that Run IS the space-efficient implementation and the alias exists only for API symmetry. Keep the AggressiveInlining alias if external API stability is required.
perf.rationale: Clarifies the API surface (Run/Try* convention) without a perf model change; reduces the chance a caller assumes RunSpaceEfficient is cheaper.
perf.risk: Removing a public method is a source-breaking API change; if external callers depend on it, keep the alias and only add documentation. No runtime behavior change either way.
